text:
maria_cs: FYI escalation from AcmeCorp — they say SCIM created the users but role assignments (Product:Editor/Viewer) are not showing up in the app. customer reports hundreds of users provisioned with no roles. ticket #ACME-4821.

sana_support: Ack. Can you paste the customer's SCIM logs (from Azure) and the request payload we received? quick check: are we seeing PATCH to /Users/<id>/groups or to /Groups?

maria_cs: Pasting stripped logs below (sensitive fields redacted). Azure shows a 200 for user create but a 400 when trying to apply group->role mapping.

```
AzureProvisioningLog: 2025-11-03T14:02:12Z POST https://scim.redwood.ai/Users 201 Created userId=usr_8741
AzureProvisioningLog: 2025-11-03T14:03:05Z PATCH https://scim.redwood.ai/Users/usr_8741 400 "InvalidRoleReference" payload={... "groups": [{"value":"Group:acme-editors","display":"Acme Editors","$ref":"/Groups/gg_123"}]}
AzureDetail: error_detail: "group externalId '/acme/editors' not found in mapping table"
```

eli_engineer: Interesting — our service maps incoming group externalIds to product roles. If externalId doesn't match (exact string) we treat as unknown group and skip role assignment. Did ACME recently change AD group names or externalId format?

maria_cs: They said they migrated from on-prem AD to Azure and admins used a script that prefixed external IDs with a leading slash. Before: `acme-editors`, after: `/acme/editors`

josh_reliability: That fits. Our group->role mapper does strict equality on externalId. Historically some customers used normalized externalIds (dashed), others used path-like externalIds. We should be tolerant. Two action options: 1) quick patch to normalize incoming externalId (trim leading/trailing slashes, collapse spaces) before lookup; 2) teach mapper to fallback to displayName fuzzy match. Option 1 is lower risk.

eli_engineer: I can ship a small change to the SCIM ingestion service to call `normalizeExternalId()` which does: lowercase, trim whitespace, remove leading/trailing `/`, replace `/` with `-`, collapse `__+` to `-`. Will add a unit test and a feature flag.

maria_cs: Customer wants prompt fix. Are we ok to deploy to prod canary then rollout?

deploy-bot: Deploy request: branch=fix/scim-externalid-normalize author=eli_engineer target=staging -> queued

kelly_account_manager: I'll message Acme and ask if they can apply a temporary mapping on their side. But they prefer we fix server-side since they have many scripts.

eli_engineer: Quick repro snippet I used locally:

```
PATCH /Users/usr_8741
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "groups": [{ "value": "Group:acme-editors", "externalId": "/acme/editors", "display": "Acme Editors" }]
}
```

// prior to patch our mapper did: lookup(externalId) -> null -> skip
// after patch: normalize('/acme/editors') -> 'acme-editors' -> match -> assign role

okta-bot: Received provisioning webhook: event=GroupUpdated group_externalId="/acme/editors" members=312

josh_reliability: Make sure we log both original externalId and normalized value for a week so we can audit. Also add a small metric for `scim.mapper.externalid_normalized` to see how many hits we get.

eli_engineer: Working on branch now. Plan: add normalization, unit tests, feature flag `scim_normalize_externalid`, canary deploy to 10% for 30m, then 100% if no regressions. Will include migration script to backfill any groups that contain slashes in the mapping table with normalized key aliases.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: env=prod canary_pct=10 feature_flag=scim_normalize_externalid

maria_cs: Customer confirmed they see a retry stream from Azure that failed earlier. We'll ask them to re-run provisioning after we flip the flag.

eli_engineer: Canary looks good so far (no 5xx, patch counts normal). Rolling to 100%. Backfill script ran, created alias keys for 27 groups for AcmeCorp.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete: env=prod success. Backfill result: created_aliases=27

kelly_account_manager: Told Acme they can retry now. They re-ran provisioning and confirmed roles are now assigned. "Huge relief" per their admin. :tada:

maria_cs: Closing loop: root cause = strict externalId equality + migration that introduced leading slashes. Fix = normalize externalIds server-side + backfill alias keys. Follow-ups: add docs note about externalId formats and SDK helper for normalization, add a runbook entry for similar incidents.

josh_reliability: +1 on runbook. Also create an alert for sudden spike in `scim.mapper.lookup_misses` so we detect other customers moving formats.

maria_cs: Thanks everyone. I'll mark the support ticket resolved and email postmortem to Acme. "Fix deployed and verified"
